items.title: [Cariboo Signals Reviews] Episode Review — Cariboo Signals, October 2, 2026
items.content_html:
What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 36982082260.

Territory check hit its lookup ceiling and kept unsupported claims

The script named Secwépemc and Tŝilhqot'in in contexts where the territory map—which links nations to specific regions—did not support those connections. Seven individual mismatches were caught and flagged. On the eighth mismatch, the pipeline hit its per-run lookup ceiling of 8 checks and stopped validating. It then encountered a sentence that kept an unsupported nation claim despite a rewrite attempt, and rather than drop the claim or loop again, it left the sentence in the script.

After hitting the ceiling, 11 more potential mismatches—place names like Mile, Ranch, Moab, Similkameen, and others—went unchecked. The listener heard a script with territory claims the pipeline could not verify and chose not to revisit.

Two TTS takes came back short; both retries still fell short

The text-to-speech engine returned 2 segments shorter than their word counts predicted. Both were retried once. Both retries still underran. The pipeline kept the longer of each pair, so nothing was dropped from the episode—but the audio for those segments does not match its scripted length.

Script expanded 708 words but still landed 490 under target

The first draft came in at 2202 words against a target of 3400. It was sent back for expansion. The rewrite added 708 words and shipped at 2910 words—still 490 short of target. The pipeline did not loop a second time to close the gap.

All roundup citations aligned; no deep-dive citations did

The roundup section matched all 15 of its source citations to articles in the pool. The three deep-dive stories—on B.C. wildfire cultural burns, conservation officer warnings, and municipal campaign harassment—yielded zero matched citations. Where a citation exists in the facts, the pipeline found it in the roundup. Where it did not, it found nothing in the deep dives.

One asset missing from R2 storage will 404 for crawlers

An object referenced by the podcast feed XML does not exist in Cloudflare R2 and cannot be recovered from disk. When crawlers request it, they will receive a 404. The feed went live anyway.

No AI-tell patterns detected; voice ratio 0.83 Casey to Riley

The script passed quality checks for generated-text patterns. Casey spoke 0.83 times as much as Riley. The episode ran 17 minutes 20 seconds of audio (15.8 MB) and video (60.3 MB). All three scheduled runs completed on time: primary at 1:05 AM Pacific finished at 1:27 AM, fallback 1 at 2:05 AM, and fallback 2 (this review's run) at 3:05 AM. The pipeline made 15 API calls to Claude, 11 to Brave Search, and 5 to Brave Answers, using 42,074 input tokens. Episode 247 is now in the RSS feed.

items.content_html:
What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke.

Two runs failed before this one started

The primary run at 1:05 AM Pacific and its fallback at 2:05 AM both completed but concluded as failures. The script generation step failed in both cases after 92 seconds of work. This run — Fallback 2, triggered at 3:05 AM Pacific — is executing now.

Script generation failed twice, then succeeded here

The Generate episode script step broke the first two attempts. The facts do not state what caused the breakage. This run's script generation completed successfully, taking 92 seconds as well.

The script came in short and was expanded

The first draft delivered 2001 words against a target of 3400 words. The pipeline sent it back for an expand pass rather than shipping it undersized. The final script reflects that revision cycle.

Three deep dives made the cut

The episode carries stories from Quartz on power generation economics, APTN News on Mark Carney and economic reconciliation, and RealAgriculture on plant breeding strategy. That is 3 deep dives for the day.

Fifty-three stories were dropped by design

The roundup pool held 53 more stories than the airtime budget allows in a single segment. Those stories remain eligible to surface on better-matched days. This is the intended behavior of the NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT constraint.

No other warnings flagged

The run produced no anomalies outside script length and the earlier failures.
